title: No Domestic COVID Vaccine Passports Bill 2021
short_title: No Domestic COVID Vaccine Passports Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit domestic COVID vaccine passports and discrimination based on COVID vaccination status across government services, employment, businesses, education, accommodation and voluntary organisations.
Requesting or requiring a vaccine passport would itself count as discrimination, and the rules would cover access to goods, services, premises and voluntary activities.

Exceptions would permit compliance with foreign laws and disclosure of vaccination information to courts, hospitals or medical practitioners, with a separate exception concerning state officers and employees.
changes: Employers would be prohibited from discriminating against workers because of COVID vaccination status.
The Commonwealth and territories could not fund, license or contract with specified entities reasonably likely to discriminate on that basis.
The prohibitions would override conflicting Commonwealth, state and territory laws.
The legislation would extend to Australia's external territories.
summary.affected: Governments, employers, businesses, voluntary bodies and people whose COVID vaccination status affects their treatment are affected.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The speaker introduced the No Domestic COVID Vaccine Passports Bill 2021, arguing that COVID vaccines should be voluntary and opposing domestic vaccine passports, citing US data showing over 2,600 hospitalised breakthrough cases and nearly 550 deaths among fully vaccinated individuals as of 14 June, as well as concerns about vaccine safety and discrimination against Paralympians.
